newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sees Peru's trade bloc exit as positive.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sees Peru's trade bloc exit as positive.

text.p: Peru's withdrawal from the Andean Group is a positive development that will bring more coherence to the South American trade bloc, a Venezuelan government minister said on Tuesday.

"It will give us a stronger image in dealing with the European Union and the trade and financial international community," External Trade Minister Freddy Rojas said. "We'll be more homogeneous and more coherent because we now all form part of a free-trade zone," he told an economic forum.
Peru formally announced its withdrawal from the Andean Group last Friday, ending a 28-year association with the four other members: Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela.
Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said his decision to withdraw reflected irreconcilable differences with other members, in particular over export tariffs.

Rojas said Peru's departure, which followed Chile's withdrawal in 1976, would give the Andean Group more leverage to negotiate an association with the Mercosur trade bloc, composed of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. Chile is an associate member of Mercosur.
Venezuelan Foreign Minister Miguel Angel Burelli agreed the Andean trade group would emerge as a more cohesive force.
He told reporters that an Andean Group summit meeting next week in Sucre, Bolivia, would begin an "immediate mend of this community that will now be stronger."
